text:
Oliver Bjorkstrand has six goals for the Rangers playing barely 11 and a half minutes a night, an efficient 2.73 points per 60 minutes. He's on the second power-play unit and a third line with Will Cuylle, and he's scored four times in his last ten games.

Here's the catch: he's shooting 20.7%, against about 12.6% for a typical Bjorkstrand season, and that gap is most of the story. Evolving-Hockey had him at 0.3 wins last season, with the power play doing the lifting and his even-strength offense in the bottom 10% of forwards. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that he rarely carries the puck in (35% of his entries), so his line lives on dump-ins and the forecheck. None of that makes him bad. It makes him a useful depth winger on a heater. Our range has him at about 18 goals by April, which would still be a good year; just don't expect the pace to hold.
